question: Donald Trump’s Executive Order 14168 of 20 January 2025 may affect the ability of transgender, intersex and non-binary people from the EU to enter the United States. What steps has the Commission taken or does it plan to take vis-à-vis the US administration to ensure that people from the EU whose passports do not reflect their gender of assignment at birth are not prevented from entering the US for that reason or are not forced to come out or have incorrect information entered into their passport?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (23.6.2025) Passports issued by EU Member States adhere to globally interoperable standards adopted by the International Civil Aviation Organization1, including rules on specifying the sex of the holder. Nevertheless, States remain free to impose rules on entry, immigration and documents that are accepted for those purposes.

The Commission remains committed to achieving a Union of Equality, promoting equality, diversity and inclusion for all, notably through the LGBTIQ2 Equality Strategy 2020-20253, which pays particular attention to trans, non-binary and intersex persons. As announced in the Commission President’s Political Guidelines4 and in the 2025 Commission Work Programme5, the LGBTIQ Equality Strategy will be renewed beyond 2025.
